overview: Scoping review of methods choices in test-negative studies of seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness, following JBI methods and reported with PRISMA-ScR, under registered protocol OSR-2026-7731.
population: Test-negative studies of seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness published from 2010 onward in any language the library can translate, in any setting.
exposure: Not applicable; the concept is the set of methods choices each study made.
procedures: The library searches four bibliographic databases and two preprint servers; the registrar screens titles, abstracts and full texts, with a university reviewer double-screening 20 percent; a piloted charting form records each methods choice as made, not made or not reported; one email per study for unreported choices.

outcomes.name: Methods choices charted per study
outcomes.measure: For each study: case definition, test type, specimen timing, calendar-time handling, repeat-test handling, prior vaccination, vaccination source and SARS-CoV-2-positive controls, each coded made, not made or not reported

outcomes.name: Separate reporting for care home residents
outcomes.measure: Whether residents were included and reported separately
outcomes.why: Residents are the most exposed and least reported.

feasibility: About 2,400 titles, 250 full texts and 150 included studies fit a registrar's three months with library support.
biasMitigation: Not reported coded separately from not done

biasFlags.label: Reporting is not practice
biasFlags.note: Unreported choices may have been made; one email per study limits this.

parsimony.simplestPath: One charting form, descriptive map, no pooling.

theoreticalFramework: The design's assumptions (from the methods overview) organise the charting items; no other framework.
summary: Registered scoping review with one charting outcome and double screening.
